findings.reason: the followup is the driving artifact a coordinator reads (§05 invocation `/reckon-build … §14`), so a builder briefed from it would add the code review to the promotion payloads, which the section itself states would roll the landing back because `store_committed_review` refuses a record naming neither a run nor a plan.
findings.text: the followup f-tcirbn-s14 name and body say §14 "stores and commits a code review when it promotes", but the section was rewritten (commit 388794951) to say the opposite: "The promotion commit's review payloads do not change… The code review stays in the staging store… Committing code reviews to the tree is a separate decision and not part of this section"

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every cited anchor resolves: `_staging_review_record_by_run` (reckon/crew/promotion_checks.py:1804), `_plan_review_record_for_promoting_run` (promotion_checks.py:1830), `code_review_identity` (reckon/crew/review_dispositions.py:272), `store_committed_review` (reckon/crew/review.py:2584), `names_a_review_subject` (review.py:1756), `delivered_report_record` (reckon/crew/plan_review.py:2069), `list_code_reviews` (plan_review.py:2854), the harness `tests/test_a_queued_plan_review_is_stored.py`, and the composed run id `r-20261015T053316274650-review-code-a8eb488cc578` which is the `review_run_id` the nova sidecar `reports/nova/code-review/a8eb488cc578/code-review.json` carries.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §14's done-when is measurable and declares a negative control ("removes the code-review branch, and the first case must then fail"), and its six cases assert observable store/record state rather than a suite that passes either way.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — each run is logged "under the run directory with its command, its revision and an EXIT= line", and the gate log lives on a durable path, not a scratchpad.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan label, ticket number or version tag reaches a symbol, filename or comment; the test and prompt names describe the mechanism.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §14's evidence and mechanism hold (a code-review record carries no `reviewed_run_id` and no `plan_slug`, so `names_a_review_subject` rejects it and `store_committed_review` would roll the landing back; the neighbourhood key `code_review_identity` reads from the promoting run id resolves the `code-review.json` sidecar by report directory name; the caller `_staging_review_record_by_run` is named and reachable from promotion.py:2053), but the plan's own driving followup, f-tcirbn-s14, still states the deliverable the section was rewritten to refute.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §14 carries one deliverable (a promoted code review is stored).
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §14 names its prerequisites (§6 code-review verb, §13 package choice) in prose and declares no depends-on of its own; the section's only cross-plan dependency already landed, so no missing relationship changes the section.
